# A `map` or `filter` in a branch runs only where the branch is taken, on
# every target.
#
# Go has no map or filter of its own, so each becomes a loop written before
# the statement that reads it. One in a ternary's branch, a match's arm or the
# right side of `&&` or `||` was written before the whole expression, so it
# ran whichever way the condition went: `b != null ? b.items.map(f) : []`
# read `b.items` with `b` null, and `rows[n]` in an arm the match did not
# take read past the end of the list. Now the loop is written inside the
# branch, and the expression's value is a temp each branch sets.

sngl test --platform=none app.sngl
stdout 'ok +1 tests, 0 failures'
sngl test --platform=html app.sngl
stdout 'ok +1 tests, 0 failures'
sngl test --platform=bubbletea --language=go app.sngl
stdout 'ok +1 tests, 0 failures'
sngl test --platform=fyne --language=go app.sngl
stdout 'ok +1 tests, 0 failures'
sngl test --platform=gtk4 --language=go app.sngl
stdout 'ok +1 tests, 0 failures'
sngl test --platform=android --language=kotlin app.sngl
stdout 'ok +1 tests, 0 failures'

-- app.sngl --
import ui "sngl:ui"
import test "sngl:test"

struct Box {
    items list[int]
}

component main ui.node {
    var box option[Box] = null
    var at = 3

    ui.text(value="{doubled(box).length()}")
}

// The items doubled, none where there is no box.
func doubled(b option[Box]) list[int] {
    return b != null ? b.items.map(func(i int) => i * 2) : []
}

// Whether the box holds an even item.
func holdsEven(b option[Box]) => b != null && b.items.filter(func(i int) => i % 2 == 0).length() > 0

// Whether there is no box or it holds an odd item.
func emptyOrOdd(b option[Box]) => b == null || b.items.filter(func(i int) => i % 2 == 1).length() > 0

const rows = [[1, 2]]

// Row `n` doubled, none past the first.
func row(n int) list[int] {
    return match n {
        0 => rows[n].map(func(i int) => i * 2)
        else => []
    }
}

func testBranchesRunWhereTaken(t test.Test, c main) {
    t.assert(doubled(c.box).length() == 0)
    t.assert(!holdsEven(c.box))
    t.assert(emptyOrOdd(c.box))
    t.assert(row(c.at).length() == 0)
    c.box = Box{items=[1, 2]}
    c.at = 0
    t.assert(doubled(c.box).length() == 2 && doubled(c.box)[1] == 4)
    t.assert(holdsEven(c.box))
    t.assert(emptyOrOdd(c.box))
    t.assert(row(c.at).length() == 2)
}
